articles.title: Joint Statement of the Government of Canada and the Bank of Canada on the Renewal of the Monetary Policy Framework
articles.expand: The Government and the Bank agree that monetary policy must work to promote the economic and financial well-being of Canadians. We also agree that the best way monetary policy can do this is by keeping inflation low, stable and predictable, thereby protecting Canadians from large increases in the cost of living.

articles.title: Erik Thedéen: Simplify banking regulations – without compromising resilience
articles.expand: There is great value in simplifying the current extensive regulatory framework for banks, but the reforms must not be carried out at the expense of financial stability. That was the message Erik Thedéen, speaking as Governor of the Riksbank, emphasised at the Finance Sweden’s banking conference, when he argued in favour of a more effective regulatory framework that preserves the banks’ resilience.

articles.title: Eurozone Inflation Accelerates To 3-Year High On Energy Prices
articles.expand: Eurozone inflation accelerated to a three-year high in October on energy prices, reinforcing expectations for another interest rate hike. Inflation increased to 4.0 percent in October from 3.8 percent in September, flash data from Eurostat showed Wednesday.

articles.title: Policy rate raised to 2 per cent
articles.expand: Stronger economic activity combined with cost increases due to supply disruptions mean that inflation is expected to continue rising going forward. The Executive Board has therefore decided to raise the policy rate by 0.25 percentage points to 2 per cent. If the outlook for inflation and economic activity holds, it is likely that the policy rate will be raised further in the coming year, in line with the policy rate forecast in September.

articles.title: The Riksbank plans to finance part of the foreign currency reserve with foreign currency loans via the Swedish National Debt Office
articles.expand: To reduce currency risk on its balance sheet, the Riksbank plans to finance the equivalent of around SEK 200 billion of the foreign currency reserve with foreign currency loans via the Swedish National Debt Office. The intention is also to replace the FX swaps that the Riksbank has used for currency hedging since 2023. This change is not intended to affect the long-term size of the foreign currency reserve and does not serve any monetary policy purpose.
